titleZh: 《塔克·卡尔森今夜秀》——完整访谈
summaryEn: Elon Musk's full Fox News interview with Tucker Carlson: the dangers of AI and his plans for a 'TruthGPT', plus Twitter, free speech and government influence on social media.
summaryZh: 埃隆·马斯克在福克斯新闻接受塔克·卡尔森的完整访谈：人工智能的危险及其“TruthGPT”计划，以及 Twitter、言论自由和政府对社交媒体的影响。

segments.textEn: Artificial intelligence is one of those topics that's just spooky and sci fi enough to make for a compelling television segment. They love it on the morning shows. But at the same time, AI is complex enough that it's easy to misrepresent. It sounds like something that could be revolutionary, even dangerous to humanity. But is it? And if it is, what should we do about it? Those questions are significant enough that we wanted to find someone who could provide a definitive answer.
segments.textZh: 人工智能是那种恰好既诡异、又足够科幻，能成为引人入胜的电视节目片段的话题。晨间节目很喜欢它。但与此同时，AI 又足够复杂，很容易被错误表述。它听起来像是某种可能具有革命性、甚至对人类构成危险的东西。但真的是这样吗？如果是，我们应该怎么办？这些问题足够重大，因此我们想找一位能够给出明确答案的人。

segments.textEn: Elon Musk seemed like the right person. Musk has been thinking about AI and worrying about it for most of his life. Nearly a decade ago, he helped found a nonprofit research project called Open AI. And the point was in the name. If we're going to have artificial intelligence, and apparently we are, it ought to be open, open to the world. That would help ensure that it's used for good and not evil. That was the idea.
segments.textZh: 埃隆·马斯克似乎是合适的人选。马斯克一生中的大部分时间都在思考 AI，并为之担忧。近10年前，他协助创立了一个名为 Open AI 的非营利研究项目。而其要旨就在名称里。如果我们将会拥有人工智能，而显然我们会有，它就应当是开放的，向全世界开放。这将有助于确保它被用于善而非恶。这就是当时的理念。

segments.textEn: But as the years passed and Musk found himself preoccupied building a couple of enormous companies, SpaceX and Tesla, OpenAI got away from him. As of tonight, OpenAI is no longer open. It's not a non profit research project dedicated to using artificial intelligence to serve humanity. It is instead a commercial enterprise backed by Microsoft and controlled to some extent by the Democratic Party. Elon Musk thinks that's a problem.
segments.textZh: 但随着岁月流逝，马斯克发现自己忙于打造 SpaceX 和 Tesla 这2家巨型公司，OpenAI 逐渐脱离了他的掌控。截至今晚，OpenAI 已经不再开放。它不再是一个致力于利用人工智能服务人类的非营利研究项目。相反，它是一家由微软支持、并在一定程度上受民主党控制的商业企业。埃隆·马斯克认为这是个问题。

segments.textEn: In fact, he believes it's a threat to human civilization, tantamount to maybe even more terrifying than thermonuclear weapons. The conversation you're about to see took place recently in a hotel room in Los Angeles. We think it's important enough that we're going to play the entire thing for you over the course of tonight and tomorrow. Here's how the conversation began.
segments.textZh: 事实上，他认为这是对人类文明的威胁，堪比热核武器，甚至可能比热核武器更可怕。你们即将看到的对话最近发生在洛杉矶的一间酒店客房里。我们认为它足够重要，因此将在今晚和明天的节目中为你们播放完整对话。以下是对话的开场。

segments.textEn: So all of a sudden AI is everywhere. People who weren't quite sure what it was are playing with it on their phones. Is that good or bad?
segments.textZh: 于是，AI 突然无处不在。那些还不太确定它是什么的人，正在手机上使用它。这是好事还是坏事？

segments.textEn: Yes. So I've been thinking about AI for a long time, since I was in college. Really. It's one of the things that the sort of four or five things I thought would really affect the future dramatically. It is fundamentally profound in that the smartest creatures, as far as you know, on this earth are humans is our defining characteristic. Yes, we obviously are weaker than, say, chimpanzees, less agile, but real smarter.
segments.textZh: 是的。那么我思考 AI 已经很久了，从我上大学时开始。真的。它是我认为会真正显著影响未来的，大概4或5件事情中的1件。从根本上来说，它意义深远，因为据你所知，这个地球上最聪明的生物是人类，这是我们的决定性特征。是的，显然我们比方说黑猩猩更弱，也不那么敏捷，但真的更聪明。

segments.textEn: So now what happens when something vastly smarter than the smartest person comes along in silicon form? It's very difficult to predict what will happen in that circumstance. It's called the singularity. It's a singularity like a black hole, because you don't know what happens after that. It's hard to predict. So I think we should be cautious with AI and we should, I think there should be some government oversight because it affects the, it's a danger to the public.
segments.textZh: 那么现在，当某种远比最聪明的人更聪明的东西以硅的形态出现时，会发生什么？在那种情况下会发生什么，非常难以预测。这被称为奇点。它是一个像黑洞一样的奇点，因为你不知道在那之后会发生什么。很难预测。所以我认为我们应该谨慎对待 AI，而且我们应该，我认为应该有某种政府监管，因为它会影响……它对公众是一种危险。

segments.textEn: And so when you, when you have things that are a danger to the public, you know, like, let's say so food, food and drugs. That's why we have the Food and Drug Administration and the Federal Aviation Administration, the fcc, we have, we have these agencies to oversee things that affect the public where there could be public harm. And you don't want companies cutting corners on safety and then having people suffer as a result.
segments.textZh: 所以，当你面对那些会对公众构成危险的事物时，你知道，比如说食品、食品和药品。这就是为什么我们有食品药品监督管理局、联邦航空管理局、联邦通信委员会，我们有、我们有这些机构来监管那些会影响公众、可能造成公共伤害的事物。而且你不希望公司在安全问题上偷工减料，结果让人们因此受害。

segments.textEn: So that's why I've actually for a long time been a strong advocate of AI regulation. So that I think regulation is, you know, it's not fun to be regulated. It's, it's sort of somewhat of a, sort of arduous to be regulated. I have a lot of experience with regular regulated industries because obviously automotive is highly regulated. You can fill this room with all the regulations that are required for a production car just in the United States.
segments.textZh: 所以，实际上很长时间以来，我一直是人工智能监管的坚定倡导者。所以我认为监管是，你知道，被监管并不好玩。它、它算是有点、有点费力。我对受监管、受监管的行业很有经验，因为显然汽车行业受到高度监管。仅仅是在美国，一辆量产汽车需要遵守的所有法规，就能装满这个房间。

segments.textEn: And then there's a whole different set of, of regulations in Europe and China and the rest of the world. So very familiar with being overseen by a lot of regulators. And the same thing is true with rockets. You can't just willy nilly shoot rockets off, not big ones anyway, because the FAA oversees that.
segments.textZh: 然后欧洲和中国以及世界其他地区还有一整套完全不同的，的法规。所以我非常熟悉受到许多监管机构的监督。火箭也是如此。你不能随随便便发射火箭，无论如何，大型火箭不行，因为美国联邦航空管理局会对此进行监管。

segments.textEn: And then even to get a launch license, there are probably half a dozen or more federal agencies that need to approve it, plus state agencies. So it's, I've been through so many regulatory situations, it's insane. And you know, sometimes people think I'm some sort of like regulatory maverick that sort of defies regulators on a regular basis, but this is actually not the case. So in, you know, once in a blue moon, rarely I will disagree with regulators, but the vast majority of the time my companies agree with the regulations and comply anyway.
segments.textZh: 然后，即使只是取得发射许可证，也可能需要大约6个或更多联邦机构批准，此外还有州级机构。所以，我经历过太多监管情形了，简直疯狂。而且你知道，有时候人们认为我是某种监管独行侠，经常公然反抗监管机构，但实际情况并非如此。所以，你知道，极少数情况下，偶尔我会不同意监管机构的看法，但绝大多数时候，我的公司都认同这些法规，而且无论如何都会遵守。

segments.textEn: So I think, I think we should take this seriously and we should have a regulatory agency I think needs to start with a group that initially seeks insight into AI, then solicits opinion from industry and then has proposed rulemaking. And then those rules, you know, will probably, hopefully, grudgingly be accepted by the major players in AI. And I think we'll have a better chance of advanced AI being beneficial to humanity in that circumstance.
segments.textZh: 所以我认为、我认为我们应该认真对待这件事，而且应该设立一个监管机构。我认为需要先成立一个最初旨在深入了解人工智能的小组，然后征求业界意见，之后提出规则制定方案。然后这些规则，你知道，可能会、希望会被人工智能领域的主要参与者勉强接受。而我认为，在这种情况下，先进人工智能造福人类的机会会更大。

segments.textEn: But all regulations start with a perceived danger. Planes fall to the sky or food causes botulism. I don't think the average person playing with AI on his iPhone perceives any danger. Can you just roughly explain what you think the Dangers might be, yeah.
segments.textZh: 但所有监管都始于一种人们感知到的危险。飞机坠向天空，或者食物导致肉毒杆菌中毒。我认为，普通人在自己的 iPhone 上玩人工智能时，并不会感知到任何危险。你能不能大致解释一下，你认为危险可能是什么，是的。

segments.textEn: So the danger really AI is perhaps more dangerous than say mismanaged aircraft design or production maintenance or bad car production in the sense that it is. It has the potential, however small one may regard that probability, but it is non trivial. It has the potential of civilizational destruction. There's movies like Terminator, but it wouldn't quite happen like Terminator because the intelligence would be in the data centers.
segments.textZh: 所以真正的危险是，人工智能也许比管理不善的飞机设计、生产维护或糟糕的汽车生产更危险，就其本身而言。它有这种潜力，无论人们认为这种概率有多小，但它并非微不足道。它有摧毁文明的潜力。有《终结者》这样的电影，但事情不会完全像《终结者》那样发生，因为智能会存在于数据中心里。

segments.textEn: Right. The robot's just the end effector. But I think perhaps what you may be alluding to here is that regulations are really only put into effect after something terrible has happened.
segments.textZh: 对。机器人只是末端执行器。但我想，也许你在这里所暗示的是，监管实际上只有在某些可怕的事情发生之后才会实施。

segments.textEn: That's correct.
segments.textZh: 没错。

segments.textEn: If that's the case for AI and we only put in regulations after something terrible has happened, it may be too late to actually put the regulations in place. The AI may be in control at that point.
segments.textZh: 如果人工智能也是这样，而我们只有在某些可怕的事情发生后才实施监管，那么再真正建立监管可能就太晚了。届时人工智能可能已经掌控局面。

segments.textEn: You think that's real? It is. It is conceivable that I could take control and reach a point where you couldn't turn it off and it would be making, making the decisions for people.
segments.textZh: 你认为那是真的吗？是的。可以想象，我可能会取得控制权，并达到一个你无法将它关闭的地步，而它会替人们作出、作出决定。

segments.textEn: Yeah, absolutely.
segments.textZh: 是的，绝对如此。

segments.textEn: Absolutely.
segments.textZh: 绝对如此。

segments.textEn: No, it's that. That's definitely where things are headed for. Sure.
segments.textZh: 不，就是那样。那绝对是事情正在走向的方向。当然。

segments.textEn: I mean, things like, like say ChatGPT, which is based on GPT4 from OpenAI, which company that I played a critical role in creating, unfortunately, back when it was a nonprofit. Yes.
segments.textZh: 我的意思是，像、比如 ChatGPT 这样的东西，它基于 OpenAI 的 GPT4，而我在创立这家公司时发挥了关键作用，不幸的是，那时候它还是一家非营利机构。是的。

segments.textEn: I mean, the reason Open exists at all is that Larry Page and I used to be close friends and I would stay at his house in Palo Alto and I would talk to him late into the night about AI safety. And at least my perception was that Larry was not taking AI safety seriously enough. And what did he say about it? He really seemed to be sort of digital superintelligence, basically digital God, if you will, as soon as possible.
segments.textZh: 我的意思是，Open 之所以会存在，完全是因为拉里·佩奇和我过去是亲密朋友，我会住在他位于帕洛阿尔托的家里，并和他一直聊人工智能安全聊到深夜。而至少在我看来，拉里对人工智能安全不够认真。那他对此怎么说？他似乎真的是某种数字超级智能，基本上就是数字上帝，如果你愿意这么称呼的话，越快越好。

segments.textEn: He wanted that.
segments.textZh: 他想要那个。

segments.textEn: Yes. He's made many public statements over the years. The whole goal of Google is what's called AGI, Artificial General Intelligence or artificial superintelligence. And I agree with him that there's great potential for good, but there's also potential for bad. And so if, if you've got some radical new technology, you want to try to take set actions that maximize the probability, it will do good and minimize the probability will do bad things.
segments.textZh: 是的。这些年来，他发表过许多公开声明。Google 的整个目标就是所谓的 AGI，即通用人工智能，或者人工超级智能。而我同意他的看法，它有巨大的向善潜力，但也有作恶的潜力。所以，如果、如果你拥有某种激进的新技术，你会想设法采取一系列行动，使它做好事的概率最大化，并使它做坏事的概率最小化。

segments.textEn: Yes.
segments.textZh: 是的。

segments.textEn: It can't just be helpful.
segments.textZh: 它不可能只是有帮助。

segments.textEn: Other.
segments.textZh: 其他。

segments.textEn: Let's just go barreling forward and hope for the best. And then at one point I said, well, what about we're going to make sure humanity's okay here?
segments.textZh: 我们就这么一路猛冲向前，并祈求最好的结果。然后有一次我说，那么，我们要怎么确保人类在这里安然无恙？

segments.textEn: And.
segments.textZh: 而且。

segments.textEn: And then he called me a speciast.
segments.textZh: 然后他称我是一个 speciast。

segments.textEn: Did he use that term?
segments.textZh: 他用了那个词吗？

segments.textEn: Yes. And there were witnesses. I wasn't the only one there when he called me a specist. And so I was like, okay, that's it. Yes, I'm a specist. Okay, you got me. What are you?
segments.textZh: 是的。而且有目击者。他称我是 specist 时，在场的不只有我。所以我当时想，好吧，就这样吧。是的，我是 specist。好吧，被你逮到了。那你是什么？

segments.textEn: Yeah, I'm fully a speciesist. Busted.
segments.textZh: 是啊，我完全是个物种主义者。被逮个正着。

segments.textEn: So that was the last draw. At the time, Google had acquired DeepMind. And so Google, DeepMind together had about 3/4 of all the talent in the world. They obviously had a tremendous amount of money and more computers than anyone else. So I'm like, okay, we have a unipolar world here where there's just one, one company that has close to a monopoly on AI talent and computers like scale computing. And person who's in charge doesn't seem to care.
segments.textZh: 所以那是最后一次抽签。当时，Google 已经收购了 DeepMind。因此，Google 和 DeepMind 加起来拥有全世界大约 3/4 的人才。他们显然拥有巨额资金，而且计算机比任何其他人都多。所以我当时想，好吧，我们这里是一个单极世界，只有一、一个公司几乎垄断了人工智能人才和计算机，比如规模化计算。而负责人似乎并不在乎。

segments.textEn: Safety.
segments.textZh: 安全。

segments.textEn: This is not good. So then I thought, what's the furthest thing from Google would be like a nonprofit that is fully open? Because Google is closed for profit. So that's why the open and open air force open source, you know, transparency. So people know what's going on.
segments.textZh: 这不好。所以后来我想，与 Google 相距最远的东西会是什么，比如一家完全开放的非营利机构？因为 Google 是封闭的营利机构。所以这就是为什么要开放，以及开放空军、开源，你知道，透明。这样人们就知道正在发生什么。

segments.textEn: Yes.
segments.textZh: 是的。

segments.textEn: And that we don't want to have like a. I mean, while I'm normally in favor of for profit, we don't want this to be sort of a profit maximizing demon from hell that just never stops.
segments.textZh: 而且我们不希望出现一种……我的意思是，虽然我通常赞成营利，但我们不希望它变成某种来自地狱、追求利润最大化而且永不停歇的恶魔。

segments.textEn: Right.
segments.textZh: 对。

segments.textEn: So that's how OpenAI.
segments.textZh: 所以 OpenAI 就是这样。

segments.textEn: So you want species incentives here, Incentives that.
segments.textZh: 所以你希望这里有物种激励，激励措施。

segments.textEn: Yes, I think we want, we want pro human. Yeah, let's make the future good for the humans. Yes, yes. Because we're humans.
segments.textZh: 是的，我认为我们想要，我们想要亲人类的。是啊，让我们让未来对人类有利。是的，是的。因为我们是人类。

segments.textEn: So can you just put it. I keep pressing, but just, just for people who haven't thought this through and aren't familiar with it. And the cool parts of, of artificial intelligence are so obvious, you know, write your college paper for you. Write a limerick about yourself. There's a lot there that's fun and useful, but can you be more precise about what's potentially dangerous and scary? Like what could it do? What specifically are you worried about going
segments.textZh: 所以你能不能直接说清楚。我一直在追问，但只是，只是为了那些还没有仔细思考过这件事、也不熟悉它的人。人工智能很酷的那些部分如此显而易见，你知道，替你写大学论文。写一首关于你自己的五行打油诗。它有很多有趣而且有用的东西，但你能不能更具体地说明，哪些方面可能危险、令人害怕？比如它能做什么？你具体担心会发生什么

segments.textEn: with old sayings, the pen is mightier than the sword. So if you have a super intelligent AI that is capable of writing incredibly well and in a way that is very influential, you know, convincing. And then is constantly figuring out what is more convincing to people over time. And then enter social media, for example, Twitter, but also Facebook and others, you know, and potentially manipulates public opinion in a way that is very bad.
segments.textZh: 用一句老话来说，笔比剑更有力量。所以，如果你有一个超级智能 AI，它能够写得极其出色，而且写作方式非常有影响力，你知道，很有说服力。然后它还在不断弄清楚，随着时间推移，什么对人们更有说服力。然后再进入社交媒体，比如 Twitter，还有 Facebook 等其他平台，你知道，并且可能以一种非常糟糕的方式操纵公众舆论。

segments.textEn: How would we even know?
segments.textZh: 我们甚至怎么会知道？

segments.textEn: How do we even know? So to sum up in the words of Elon Musk, for all human history, human beings have been the smartest beings on the planet. Now human beings have created something that is far smarter than they are, and the consequences of that are impossible to predict. And the people who created it don't care. In fact, as he put it, Google founder Larry Page, a former friend of his, is looking to build a, quote, digital God and believes that anybody who's worried about that is a species, in other words, is looking out for human beings first.
segments.textZh: 我们怎么会知道？所以，用埃隆·马斯克的话总结，在整个人类历史中，人类一直是地球上最聪明的存在。现在人类创造出了某种远比他们更聪明的东西，而其后果无法预测。创造它的人并不在乎。事实上，正如他所说，Google 创始人拉里·佩奇，他从前的朋友，正寻求打造一个，引用原话，数字上帝，并且认为任何对此感到担忧的人都是一个物种，换句话说，就是把人类放在首位。

segments.textEn: Elon Musk responded. As a human being, it's okay to look out for human beings first. And then at the end he said, the real problem with AI is not simply that it will jump the boundaries and become autonomous and you can't turn it off in the short term. The problem with AI is that it might control your brain through words. And this is the application that we need to worry about now, particularly going into the next presidential election.
segments.textZh: 埃隆·马斯克回应道。作为一个人，首先维护人类是可以的。然后在最后他说，AI 真正的问题并不只是它会突破边界、变得自主，而你短期内无法关闭它。AI 的问题在于，它可能通过文字控制你的大脑。而这正是我们现在需要担心的应用，尤其是在即将进入下一次总统选举之际。

segments.textEn: The Democratic Party, as usual, was ahead of the curve on this. They've been thinking about how to harness AI for political power. More on that next.
segments.textZh: 民主党一如既往，在这件事上走在了前面。他们一直在思考如何利用 AI 获取政治权力。接下来会有更多内容。

segments.textEn: In the long term, I may become autonomous and take over the world, but in the short term, it's being used by politicians to control what you think, to end your independent judgment and erase democracy on the eve of a presidential election. Elon Musk is very worried about that. He told us about his plan to stop it.
